o: A Foundry resource key and a SAS URL for a blob container
An OAuth 2.0 token and a managed identity endpoint URL
A client certificate and the Azure subscription ID
No credentials — the connection is anonymous by default
cards.s: Resource key + blob container SAS URL
cards.e: The connection needs both a key for the Foundry/Speech resource itself and a SAS URL so the server can read and write audio files in blob storage — two distinct credentials for two distinct responsibilities.

source.title: Develop a speech agent with the Azure Speech MCP server

By configuring the voice in the MCP server settings before connecting
By setting an environment variable in the client application code
Voice selection isn't possible through an agent, only through the raw SDK
cards.s: Name the voice in your prompt

Through the Azure portal's networking blade

Close and reopen the WebRTC connection

cards.q: Which kind of model can you use to respond to visual input?
cards.e: Multimodal models accept image input alongside text and reason over both. Embedding models produce vectors for similarity search — they don't 'respond' to a visual prompt in conversation.

source.title: Develop a vision-enabled generative AI application

cards.q: How can you submit a prompt that asks a model to analyze an image?
o: Submit a prompt that contains a multi-part user message, containing both text content and image content
Submit one prompt with an image-based message followed by another prompt with a text-based message
Submit the image as the system message and the instruction as the user message
Upload the image as a separate file attachment outside the message array
cards.s: One multi-part user message: text + image
cards.e: A single user message can carry multiple content parts — text and image together — so the model sees both in the same turn, rather than needing two separate prompts or misusing the system message for image content.

source.title: Develop a vision-enabled generative AI application

cards.q: How can you include an image in a message?
o: As a URL or as binary data
Only by referencing an uploaded file ID
cards.e: Multimodal messages accept an image either by reference (a URL) or inline as binary/base64 data — both paths are supported, not just one.

source.title: Develop a vision-enabled generative AI application

cards.q: You want to find a model in Microsoft Foundry to generate images. Which inference task should you filter by?
cards.e: Image-generation models are catalogued under the text-to-image inference task — the direction from a written prompt to a picture. Image-to-text is the reverse (captioning), a different task filter entirely.

cards.q: Which OpenAI API can you use with image-generation models?
cards.e: Image-generation models are called through the dedicated Image API. Video generation has its own separate API surface, and there's no generic 'Graphics' API.

cards.e: Sora 2 in Foundry generates clips at fixed duration options — 4, 8, or 12 seconds — rather than an arbitrary continuous range.

The image must be smaller than 1 MB
The image must contain at least one human face
The image must be in PNG format specifically

o: Making targeted adjustments to an existing video without regenerating from scratch
Combining multiple videos into one longer clip
Adding background music to generated videos
Converting a video into a series of still images

To connect Content Understanding to Azure storage
To filter out harmful content from images

cards.e: Grounding points to exactly where in the content — which region of an image, frame, or page — an extracted value came from, which is what makes human review and audit practical.

The extraction failed and needs manual review
The field was classified rather than extracted

Search engines that index only plain-text web pages

The name of the resource group where the Azure service is deployed
The Azure subscription ID and tenant ID
Only the analyzer name, with no other configuration

o: As a list of strings only

cards.q: You need to extract text and table structure from a set of documents that have varying formats. You don't need to identify specific labeled fields. Which Document Intelligence model should you use?
cards.e: The layout model extracts text plus structural elements like tables, independent of a fixed field schema — a good fit for varied formats where you don't need named fields. The read model gets you text but not table structure; invoice/custom models assume a specific document type.

source.title: Extract data with Azure Document Intelligence

cards.q: You're building a custom model in Azure Document Intelligence. What training artifacts are required when training with the REST API?
o: Sample forms along with ocr.json, labels.json, and fields.json files in a blob container
Only the sample form documents in a blob container
A minimum of 100 labeled forms and a trained classifier
A pretrained model checkpoint plus a single labels.json file
cards.e: Training a custom model via the REST API needs the sample documents plus the supporting OCR, label, and field-definition JSON files together in blob storage — sample forms alone aren't enough.

source.title: Extract data with Azure Document Intelligence

cards.q: A company processes both invoices and receipts. They want a single endpoint that routes each document to the correct extraction model. What should they use?
o: A composed model or a custom classifier paired with extraction models
A custom neural model trained on both document types combined
A prebuilt read model applied to every document
Two separate applications, one per document type
cards.s: A composed model / classifier + extraction models
cards.e: Composed models (or a classifier in front of dedicated extraction models) route each incoming document to the right extraction model automatically behind one endpoint — cleaner than merging document types into a single custom model or maintaining separate apps.

cards.q: Which component of an Azure AI Search solution is scheduled to extract and enrich data to populate an index?
o: Skillset alone, with no scheduling component
cards.e: The indexer is the component that runs (on a schedule or on demand) to pull data from a source, run enrichment, and populate the index. Projections shape enriched output for storage; queries happen after the index already exists.
